newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps gain on Iraq/UN, mogas up $4.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps gain on Iraq/UN, mogas up $4.

text.p: European oil swaps strengthened on Monday as the energy complex took note of tension between the United Nations and Iraq and opted for a bullish tint.

The U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution over the weekend threatening Iraq with further sanctions if it does not allow arms inspectors to search sensitive sites. The Council also suspended, until the end of October, the regular 60 day reviews of current sanctions.
But the hype may be a touch overdone since the threatened sanctions were not aimed directly at the recently renewed $2 billion oil-for-food deal between the U.N. and Iraq.

Brent CFDs gained about 10-12 cents on prompt dates and much less further out. Dealers said June 23-27 was pegged at -22/23 cents against August Brent from -35 cents on Friday while June 20-July 4 only firmed a touch to -32 from -35 cents. July 7-11 was almost flat at -33 cents against Brent and July 14-18 moved up a couple of cents to -33 cents.
Gasoline swaps firmed by about $4 with July moving up to $182 from $178 with August slipping into backwardation at $181.50 from Friday's slim contango.
Gas oil crack spreads were steady to a touch easier with 4Q at $4.40 from $4.40-4.45 while 1Q98 was put at $4.55, about 10 cents off Friday's levels, while 2Q98 was steady around $4.10.
Heavy fuel tracked up to $1 higher with July pegged around $82.75 with August retained a 75 cent or so contango. Dealers said activity was fairly slow in the morning.
Naphtha swaps gained about $1 with July pegged at $175 and August displaying a contango of $1 or so. September was a further $1 stronger, but nothing was heard done in the morning.
